newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Shenzhen B shares end lower, A shares up.
newsitem.headline: Shenzhen B shares end lower, A shares up.

text.p: Shenzhen's B share index closed lower on Tuesday, with investors largely staying on the sidelines and monitoring Dadonghai Tourism Centre (Holdings) Co Ltd's debut, brokers said.
The B share index lost 0.75 of a point, or 0.82 percent, to close at 89.98 on turnover of HK$24.33 million, compared with HK$12.55 million on Monday.
Light profit-taking following the index's gains for four straight sessions also weighed on the market, brokers said.
"There were signs that some Chinese investors liquidated their B share holdings to buy class A stock that are performing well," said He Ming, a broker at China Southern Securities.

Tellus Machinery was the biggest loser, falling HK$0.29 or 16.67 percent, to HK$1.45 on thin trade of 8,120 shares. Jiangling Motors dropped HK$0.10, or 5.56 percent, to HK$1.70, with 42,200 shares traded.
Lizhu Pharmaceutical, the best performer on Monday, fell back HK$0.16, or 5.42 percent, to HK$2.79 on Tuesday.

Dadonghai, which listed 80 million B shares in Shenzhen on Tuesday, opened at an intraday high of HK$1.35 and closed at HK$1.28, up 4.92 percent over its offer price of HK$1.22. It hit a low of HK$1.25 on a trade of 7.39 million shares.
Shenzhen-based brokers said Dadonghai's debut was aided by buying triggered by investor interest in its low offer price.

The A share market maintained its upward trend Tuesday, fueled in part by a report in the Shanghai Securities News that Beijing was considering a further cut in bank loan interest rates, brokers said.
The A share index rose 7.23 points, or 2.41 percent, to end at its 1996 high of 307.34, with turnover swelling to 9.85 billion yuan from 9.10 billion yuan the previous session.
The composite index gained 6.27 points, or 2.22 percent, to finish at 288.55.

Retailer Inner Mongolia National Market (Group) Co Ltd, which listed 16 million class A shares and 2.50 million staff shares in Shenzhen on Tuesday, closed its first trading session at 10.60 yuan on trade of 10.55 million shares.
The A shares were offered at 6.48 yuan per share last month, while the staff shares were issued at one yuan per share in 1992.
